description: Original eulerian_trail mod.rs with independent finite checks and typed models.
state: Finite ordered undirected multigraph Edge {u: usize, v: usize} inputs and vertex count V; successful allocations and representable materialized vectors.
cost: O(V+E) time and O(V+E) auxiliary space. Each adjacency entry is consumed at most once; output scan/reversal is linear. No call-stack recursion. Validating endpoints costs O(E) before allocating V adjacency lists. Allocation failure is outside the model.
forward: Use bridges::adjacency for complete endpoint validation before existence decisions. Empty edges return Some(Trail([],[])) if V=0 and Some(Trail([0],[])) otherwise. For nonempty edges require zero or two odd-degree vertices. Start at the smallest odd vertex, otherwise the smallest incident vertex. Iterative Hierholzer scans adjacency in input edge order, marks each edge identity once, and collects vertices and incoming edges on stack exit; reverse both. Return None if collected edge count differs from E, thereby excluding disconnected edge support.
inverse: Let U be declared inputs crossed with all returned Result values, and R the forward specification relation. C=U minus R includes wrong separator memberships, malformed/noncanonical trails, wrong existence decisions and incorrect first-error details. This is an exact specification complement, with only partial source-derived correspondence to actual Rust; no complement guarantee follows merely from a forward approximation.

For output y retain Pre(y)={G | R(G,y)} with all compatible V, ordered edges and orientation choices. Separator vectors constrain deletion connectivity rather than recover a unique graph. Euler outputs constrain identity-specific incidences and deterministic traversal; None retains all non-Eulerian valid graphs. Error fibers retain all inputs whose first invalid endpoint equals the reported edge, vertex and V.
limitations: Finite checks are not unrestricted proof.
Partial syntax has no macro expansion or semantic resolution.
Executable approximate categorical semantics are not defined.
